Shape k-means for real landmark arrays

Source: R/shape_kmeans.R
shape_kmeans.Rd

Lloyd's algorithm for clustering configurations of \(k\) landmarks in two or three dimensions. Observations are assigned to the nearest center in shape space and each center is then replaced by the mean shape of its cluster, with several random restarts.

Usage

shape_kmeans(
  X,
  K,
  mean = c("procrustes", "phi"),
  alg_steps = 10L,
  niter = 10L,
  tol = 1e-04,
  distance = c("rho", "dF", "dP")
)

Arguments

X

Numeric array of dimension \(k \times m \times n\), with \(m\) equal to 2 or 3.

K

Number of clusters (>= 2).

mean

Mean shape used to update the centers: "procrustes" (full Procrustes mean, as shapes::procGPA(); default) or "phi" (MDS mean, as shapes::MDSshape()). See shape_mean.

alg_steps

Maximum number of Lloyd steps per restart (default 10).

niter

Number of random restarts (default 10).

tol

Stopping rule: a restart stops when the relative decrease of the objective between two steps is below tol (default 1e-4).

distance

Distance in which the objective is measured, one of "rho" (default), "dF" or "dP". All three are increasing functions of the same cosine, so assignments do not depend on this choice; the objective value and the stopping rule do.

Value

A list with components:

cluster

Integer vector of length n, values in 1:K.

centers

Numeric array \(k \times m \times K\) with the cluster means, each centered with unit norm.

objective

Mean squared distance between each observation and the center it was assigned to, at the step that gave the returned clustering (the centers in force at the start of that step).

n_iter

Index of the Lloyd step, within the restart that gave the returned clustering, at which the objective was lowest.

initials

List with the K observations drawn as initial centers in each restart.

mean, distance

The options used.

Details

The algorithm follows LloydShapes() of the scripts used for the 3D bagging study. Initial centers are K observations drawn with sample.int() at the start of each restart. In each step every observation goes to its nearest center (max.col() with random tie breaking, as in the scripts), the centers are updated, and the objective is evaluated with the distances of the assignment step, i.e. before the update. The clustering and centers kept are those of the step with the lowest objective over all steps of all restarts. A cluster with a single member has that member as its center. If a cluster becomes empty its center is left unchanged (the script stops with an error in that case). Reflections are not removed (see shape_distance).

The caller's random-number stream is advanced; use set.seed() for reproducibility.

References

Dryden, I. L. and Mardia, K. V. (2016). Statistical Shape Analysis, with Applications in R, 2nd ed. Wiley.

See also

shape_mean, bagclust1 with base = "kmeans".

Examples

sim <- sim_shapes3d(n = 10, sigma = 0.5, seed = 1)
set.seed(1)
fit <- shape_kmeans(sim$X, K = 2)
table(fit$cluster, sim$group)
#>    
#>      1  2
#>   1  0 10
#>   2 10  0
fit$objective
#> [1] 0.004469681
